a.name: Standard GenAI feedback (ChatGPT-4)
a.description: General-purpose ChatGPT-4 supplies open-ended responses to general prompts and permits unstructured exploration. All participants experienced this condition in the crossover. The paper prints an overall final sample but no separate condition-specific analyzed count. PDF p. 5 (printed p. 169), GenAI feedback conditions; PDF pp. 8-9 (printed pp. 172-173), Procedure and Figure 3.

a.name: Personalised GenAI feedback (Mr. Ranedeer)
a.description: GPT-4-based Mr. Ranedeer uses configured learner preferences to generate a personalised learning plan and adapt feedback, including heuristic questions and substantive improvement suggestions. All participants experienced this condition in the crossover. The paper prints an overall final sample but no separate condition-specific analyzed count. PDF p. 5 (printed p. 169), GenAI feedback conditions; PDF pp. 8-9 (printed pp. 172-173), Procedure and Figure 3; Appendix Tables A1-A2, PDF pp. 20-21 (printed pp. 184-185).

b.name: Standard GenAI feedback (ChatGPT-4)
b.description: General-purpose ChatGPT-4 supplies open-ended responses to general prompts, supporting unstructured exploration. All participants experience this condition in the crossover. The analyzed count denotes the final study cohort exposed to this condition; outcome-specific valid-pair counts are not printed. Sources: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 169), Participants and GenAI feedback conditions; PDF p. 8 (printed p. 172), Procedure.

b.name: Personalised GenAI feedback (Mr. Ranedeer)
b.description: GPT-4-based Mr. Ranedeer uses configured knowledge level, learning style, tone and communication style to generate a personalised learning plan and adapt feedback and scaffolding. All participants experience this condition in the crossover; its analyzed count is the same final cohort as in the standard condition. Sources: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 169), Participants and GenAI feedback conditions; PDF p. 8 (printed p. 172), Procedure; Appendix Tables A1-A2, PDF pp. 20-21 (printed pp. 184-185).
